source.title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems

accepted.question_text: For the Dirichlet problem −Δu + 1/u^α = λ f(x) in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, in the regime 0 < α < 1 where maximal positive solutions are known to exist for sufficiently large λ, do there also exist additional solutions beyond the maximal positive branch, either other positive solutions or free-boundary/compact-support solutions?

evidence.quote: It is easy to show that there are no solutions for λ > 0 small enough, but it remains the problem of the possible existence of more solutions, either positive or with compact support.

accepted.question_text: For the radial singular elliptic problem −Δu + 1/u^α = λu^p in the ball B_r(0), where earlier work described two radial positive-solution branches for λ* < λ < λ** and only the upper branch beyond λ**, why does the lower positive branch terminate at the parameter value λ = λ**?

evidence.quote: Here we have a complete description of radial solutions, and we may ask why the branch “stops” at the value λ = λ∗∗.

accepted.question_text: In the one-dimensional p-Laplacian boundary-value problem −(|u′|^{p−2}u′)′ = f(u) on (−1,1) with u(±1)=0, specialized to nonlinearities such as f(u)=λu^β−u^α with −1 < α < β < p−1 and in the parameter regime corresponding to condition (4.2), is there a unique critical exponent α* such that the problem has exactly one solution on one side of α* and exactly two solutions on the other side, as conjectured by the authors?

evidence.quote: It is reasonable to guess that there should be a unique α∗ such that there is only one solution on (−1, α∗] and two on (α∗, −1/p+1). We were unable to prove that this happens in general, but this is the case if the condition β = 1 + 2α is satisfied.

accepted.question_text: For the star-shaped-domain problem −Δu + u^α = λu^β in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, 0 < α < β < 1, and N > 2(1+α)(1+β)/((1−α)(1−β)), Ilyasov and Egorov construct a positive solution w_λ > 0 satisfying ∂w_λ/∂n ≠ 0 on ∂Ω. Must this first solution in fact satisfy the sign condition ∂w_λ/∂n ≤ 0 on ∂Ω?

evidence.quote: (i) there exists a solution wλ > 0 such that ∂wλ/∂n 6= 0 on ∂Ω,
One could think that in the first case we actually have ∂wλ/∂n ≤ 0 on ∂Ω and in the second uλ > 0.

accepted.question_text: Under the same assumptions, Ilyasov and Egorov also construct a nonnegative solution u_λ ≥ 0 with ∂u_λ/∂n = 0 on ∂Ω. Is this second solution necessarily strictly positive in Ω?

evidence.quote: (ii) there exists a solution uλ ≥ 0 such that ∂uλ/∂n = 0 on ∂Ω.
One could think that in the first case we actually have ∂wλ/∂n ≤ 0 on ∂Ω and in the second uλ > 0.

accepted.question_text: In Montenegro’s approximation scheme for problem (II), smooth approximating problems produce two different nonnegative limit solutions u ≥ 0 and v ≥ 0 as ε → 0. Is the first limit solution u necessarily strictly positive in Ω?

evidence.quote: Then he proves that this functional has a minimum uϵ ≥ 0 and also a second critical point vϵ ≥ 0 (obtained by using the Mountain Pass Theorem) and that when ϵ goes to 0 they tend to (again different) solutions u ≥ 0 and v ≥ 0.
One can guess that u > 0 and that maybe v has compact support, but this is not proved in the paper.

accepted.question_text: In the same approximation framework for problem (II), does the second limit solution v necessarily have compact support, rather than being positive throughout Ω?

evidence.quote: Then he proves that this functional has a minimum uϵ ≥ 0 and also a second critical point vϵ ≥ 0 (obtained by using the Mountain Pass Theorem) and that when ϵ goes to 0 they tend to (again different) solutions u ≥ 0 and v ≥ 0.
One can guess that u > 0 and that maybe v has compact support, but this is not proved in the paper.

accepted.question_text: For problem (III), namely −Δu = K(x)(λu^β − u^α) in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, K(x)=d(x)^{−k}, 0<k<2, and 0<α<β<1, when k−α<1 are there multiple positive solutions rather than just a single positive branch for large λ?

evidence.quote: it would be interesting to know if there is more than one positive solution in the first case k − α < 1 and if, also in this case, there are compact support solutions. Information on the structure of the set of compact support solutions is interesting as well.

accepted.question_text: For the same problem (III) in the regime k−α<1, do compact-support solutions exist at all?

evidence.quote: it would be interesting to know if there is more than one positive solution in the first case k − α < 1 and if, also in this case, there are compact support solutions. Information on the structure of the set of compact support solutions is interesting as well.

accepted.question_text: For problem (III), what is the structure of the set of compact-support solutions when such solutions exist?

evidence.quote: it would be interesting to know if there is more than one positive solution in the first case k − α < 1 and if, also in this case, there are compact support solutions. Information on the structure of the set of compact support solutions is interesting as well.

accepted.question_text: Can multiplicity phenomena analogous to those discussed in the paper be established for diffusion operators beyond the Laplacian and p-Laplacian, including general linear second-order operators, Hamilton–Jacobi type operators, Monge–Ampère operators, bi-Laplacians, nonlinear systems, and Schrödinger systems?

evidence.quote: Multiplicity for different diffusion operators (not only a general linear second order operator or the p-Laplacian operator, but other nonlinear operators of Hamilton-Jacobi type, Monge-Amp`ere, bi-Laplacian, nonlinear systems, Schroedinger systems, etc.)

accepted.question_text: How do the existence, multiplicity, and free-boundary phenomena discussed in the paper change when measures are present in the equation, either as source terms or as coefficients of zero-order terms?

evidence.quote: Presence of measures at the equation (not only as a sourcing data but also as coefficients of zero order terms, . . . )
